text:
anya: quick handoff — I'm about to sign off, passing primary to @kevin for the overnight. two active alerts to be aware of:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-042 | partial 503s on /v1/generate (hosted) · sev2 · impacted customers: 3 · current status: investigating
anya: summary: started 45m ago after a deploy, traffic spike + degraded model server causing 503s. we rolled a temp route to alt-model to reduce surface but root cause looks like kv-cache OOM on a subset of pods.
kevin: copying. how critical is rollback? can we keep the alt-model route?
anya: keep alt-model (traffic split 80/20) — it reduced failure rate by ~70% per logs. don't rollback global deploy yet, we still need logs + heap dumps from affected nodes.
sam: I pulled logs from instance inference-prod-3 this morning — saw repeated "kv_cache resize failed" and GC pauses. attaching quick grep output: ``grep -i "kv_cache" /var/log/inference.log | tail -n 50``
maria: paging rules reminder: if error rate > 10% for >5m or customer-impacting flows fail, page SRE lead and Eng-ML on call. current error rate is ~12% over the last 10m (stackdriver).
kevin: ok i'll monitor and collect heapdumps. can someone share the runbook path?
anya: runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/oncall/kv-cache-oom.md — steps 1-6 for safe dump + restart. tl;dr: 1) capture /proc/{pid}/maps + jmap 2) scale down pod to 0 then up on same node to force clean cache if needed 3) restart router service.
kevin: got it. starting with `kubectl -n infra logs inference-prod-3 --since=30m` then `kubectl exec -it inference-prod-3 -- jmap -dump:live,format=b,file=/tmp/heapdump.hprof 1` — will upload to diag-bucket.
oncall-bot: NOTE: runbook step reminder: for heapdump >500MB use s3 multipart upload or coordinate with infra to avoid failing the upload.
kevin: collecting now. if heapdump collection takes >10m i will page @sre-lead.
sam: also check autoscaler events: `kubectl get hpa -n infra` — we saw hpa flapping during the spike, might be misconfigured target CPU thresholds.
maria: escalation matrix (short): first level = on-call primary (you), second = sre-lead (pager) if >15m or customer impact, third = eng-ml lead for model regressions. page immediately for persistent 503s on >5% of requests for high-value customers.
kevin: quick perf note — alt-model route is slightly higher latency but stable; keeping it reduces customer-visible errors. I'm going to keep the 80/20 split and continue diagnostics.
anya: coverage gap to flag: I'm out until 07:00 PT; there's no secondary assigned for 02:00-04:00 PT window because of a calendar conflict. kevin, can you request a backup from oncall rotation or ping @sam to cover that gap?
kevin: will do. sam, can you take 02:00-04:00 PT as secondary? if not, i'll escalate to ops to find coverage.
sam: I can take 02:00-03:30 but have a calendar hold at 03:30-04:15. will coordinate with @maria to extend if needed.
maria: I can float as fallback, but if incident flares >10% I will assume pager duties.
kevin: thanks — I'll update the handoff message in calendar and post a follow-up here at 01:50 PT before I step away.
anya: one last note for whoever picks up: customer-facing mitigation is to keep alt-model live and route high-priority tenants away from affected nodes. playbook section on tenant isolation: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/tenant-isolation.md
oncall-bot: DEPLOYMENT ALERT: deploy 2026.87 to inference-service completed 50m ago. linked to incident 2026-042.
kevin: action items for overnight: 1) monitor error rate dashboards (link: https://dashboards.redwood/err/503) 2) collect heapdumps from affected pods and upload 3) check HPA behavior and adjust threshold if it keeps flapping 4) page sre-lead if no improvement in 15m or on-call workload spike.
sre-lead: thx — I'm on standby. if you page me include the HPA logs, pod heapdump names, and samples of failing request ids. page via PagerDuty (PD: SRE-Lead) and add incident id 2026-042 in description.
kevin: thanks all. i'll post a brief handoff note at 01:50 PT and annotate incident timeline before I leave. :thumbsup:
